logic_template.maxtech_storage.batch_pro: Three steps in turn: the device labelled "inlet" runs until the storage labelled "batch" holds 64 cobblestone, the batch then waits 30 seconds, and "outlet" runs until "batch" is empty; then it starts again. Change the labels, item, amounts and time.
logic_template.maxtech_storage.button_mo: A button on the port labelled "outbox" moves 16 cobblestone from the network into the block that port faces.
logic_template.maxtech_storage.craft_fin: Posts a notice to the network log, the team and bound displays when a crafting job for sticks finishes.
logic_template.maxtech_storage.feed_furn: Sends raw iron to the furnaces labelled "furnaces": 8 to one as soon as it stops burning, and 16 every 30 seconds spread over those not burning. Put a port labelled "furnaces" on top of each furnace; it reads whether its furnace burns.
logic_template.maxtech_storage.keep_ever: Every 30 seconds, goes through each item of the tag c:ores and asks the crafting system for 64 of each one the network holds fewer than 1,000 of. Change the tag (or list the items), the limit and the amount; items nothing can craft are skipped.
logic_template.maxtech_storage.keep_item: A rule with inputs: when the network's count of the item drops below the amount, asks the crafting system for a batch. Adding it asks for the item, the amount and the batch; Copy with values makes more rules like it for other items.
Keep an item above an amount
logic_template.maxtech_storage.keep_stoc: When the network has fewer than 16 sticks, asks the crafting system for 32 more. Change the item, the limit and the amount.
logic_template.maxtech_storage.lamp_over: Lights the lamp labelled "lamp" while the network holds over 100 cobblestone, and turns it off again at 64. Pick your item, limits and label.
logic_template.maxtech_storage.lever_swi: A lever on the controller turns the device labelled "intake" on, and off again when the lever goes off.
Turn a device on with a lever
logic_template.maxtech_storage.low_power: Posts a notice when the network's stored energy falls below 20 percent; it can fire again once the store is back over 30 percent.
logic_template.maxtech_storage.priority_: Sets the priority of the storage labelled "bank" to the redstone strength on the controller: 15 with a lever on, 0 off.
logic_template.maxtech_storage.sensor_al: Posts a notice when the sensor labelled "chest sensor" sees more than 32 items in its block; it can fire again after it fell to 16.
maxtech_storage.configuration.alarms.cha: Whether a raised alarm is also sent as a chat line to the online players who may see the network. It always goes to the network's log and its logic remotes.
maxtech_storage.configuration.alarms.cle: A held low power or storage nearly full alarm clears only once the value is this many percent past its threshold, so a value swinging round the threshold does not raise it again and again.
Ticks an alarm that cleared stays listed, dimmed, before it goes.
maxtech_storage.configuration.alarms.low: A network's alarm panel raises low power when its stored MU is at or below this percent of its capacity.
maxtech_storage.configuration.alarms.rea: An alarm raised again within this many ticks of its last raise is listed as new but not sent to the network's log, logic remotes and chat again.
maxtech_storage.configuration.alarms.rec: While crafting jobs run, ticks between two looks for stuck crafts; no event says a machine filled up, so the panel looks on this cadence and stops once no job runs. Content changes look at how full storage is at most this often too.
maxtech_storage.configuration.alarms.sto: The alarm panel raises storage nearly full when the cells' bytes in use reach this percent.
maxtech_storage.configuration.bridges.po: Ticks between two reads of a bridged network that cannot report its changes.
maxtech_storage.configuration.bridges.re: Shortest gap in ticks between two reads of a bridged AE2 or Refined Storage network's contents after it reported a change. Higher is cheaper on busy networks; terminals lag more.
Items of its one kind a bulk drive holds at most. Bulk drives use no bytes; lowering this never deletes items, it only stops inserts into drives above it.
maxtech_storage.configuration.caps.bytes: Cell bytes the networks of one team may use together in one level; at the cap, storing into the networks stops (taking out still works). 0 turns the cap off.
maxtech_storage.configuration.caps.devic: Devices the networks of one team (research team, else owner) may hold together in one level; devices over it are turned away until room frees. 0 turns the cap off.
maxtech_storage.configuration.caps.zones: Zones the networks of one team may have together in one level; nodes past it get no route and their devices wait. 0 turns the cap off.
maxtech_storage.configuration.cells.bulk: How many times the bytes of its memory modules a bulk cell holds. A bulk cell holds one kind.
maxtech_storage.configuration.cells.casi: Add-on slots of the bulk casing.
Memory module slots of the bulk casing.
Add-on slots of the large casing.
Memory module slots of the large casing.
Add-on slots of the medium casing.
Memory module slots of the medium casing.
Add-on slots of the portable casing.
Memory module slots of the portable casing.
Add-on slots of the small casing.
Memory module slots of the small casing.
Slots each cell casing has in the cell workbench. The workbench shows at most 8 memory module and 4 add-on slots; a cell keeps parts beyond a lowered count.
maxtech_storage.configuration.cells.comp: Bytes a kind with data components (damage, enchantments, a name) costs instead.
maxtech_storage.configuration.cells.flui: mB of fluid one byte of a storage cell holds.
maxtech_storage.configuration.cells.item: Items one byte of a storage cell holds.
maxtech_storage.configuration.cells.kind: Bytes every kind of item or fluid in a cell costs, whatever its amount. Changes apply to cells inserted into a drive afterwards.
maxtech_storage.configuration.cells.memo: Bytes a memory module I adds to its cell (1 KB = 1,024 bytes).
Bytes a memory module II adds to its cell.
Bytes a memory module III adds to its cell.

maxtech_storage.configuration.cells.port: MU a portable cell's battery holds. Each item or fluid moved through its terminal costs energy like a network operation (network.energy.*).
MU per transfer a charger may put into a portable cell; a storage controller charges it in one go when a sneaking player uses the cell on it.
maxtech_storage.configuration.cells.stor: Bytes a storage block I holds (1 KB = 1,024 bytes).
Bytes a storage block II holds.
Bytes a storage block III holds.

Bytes a storage block holds, as a cell's memory does: items and fluids take bytes as in a cell. A lowered value never deletes contents; a block above it takes nothing more in. Applies when the block is next placed or loaded.
maxtech_storage.configuration.cells.tran: Operations a drive makes per tick at most while it empties a cell into its network or fills one from it; each moves one batch (network.batch) of one kind.
maxtech_storage.configuration.claims.cac: Seconds a device keeps an answer before asking again on its next use. A refused device asks again after this time, so a claim lifted or granted is picked up without polling.
maxtech_storage.configuration.claims.che: Whether devices nobody owns ask too, as an anonymous player. Off lets them work as before.
maxtech_storage.configuration.claims.ena: Whether ports, sensors, pattern providers and P2P outputs ask land claim and protection mods before using the block they face, as their owner right-clicking it. A refused device leaves that block alone. Only blocks with a block entity or an item, fluid or FE handler are asked about, since other mods also react to the right-click; plain blocks are always allowed. Placers and breakers always ask through the place and break events.
Fewest ticks between two evaluations of one condition switch, so a value that swings round its threshold cannot make the redstone output flap faster than this.

extended: tiered CPUs with partial results, resume and full job reports. classic: a job starts only when everything can be made and shows only its status.

maxtech_storage.configuration.crafting.c: Fewest ticks between two crafts one export port's crafting card requests.
Most items, or mB of fluid, one crafting card request asks for.
A step whose main output has a chance repeats until enough came out, at most this many times the crafts a guaranteed output would need.
Crafts each CPU cache block adds to one dispatch (a core alone sends one craft at a time), up to the tier's maxBatch.
Job steps a CPU core holds on its own.

maxtech_storage.configuration.crafting.d: Blocks from the network's controller (the node a crafting job is anchored at) within which its finished items can go into the requester's inventory; farther away they stay in storage.
How a crafting step is shared among pattern providers that have its pattern: fastest (earliest estimated finish), round_robin (even shares in turn) or lowest_load (fewest crafts in flight).
maxtech_storage.configuration.crafting.g: Ticks a generator provider keeps its machine switched on while nothing arrives before it reports the craft as stuck and gives the order up; the running job orders again.
maxtech_storage.configuration.crafting.p: Tree nodes one crafting plan may visit at most; a larger request fails with a clear error.
Milliseconds one crafting plan may take on its worker thread before it fails.
Pattern slots a pattern provider gains on top of its nine once its owner has the research.
Ticks between a pattern provider's looks at its machine's output while it waits for results; the machine's own change events wake it sooner.
maxtech_storage.configuration.crafting.s: Ticks a stock keeping rule waits before asking again after its craft was refused or failed.
maxtech_storage.configuration.crafting.t: MU a crafting tablet holds. It charges in any FE charger; an empty tablet does not open.
MU a crafting tablet spends each time it takes items from the network, stores items in it or requests a crafting job, on top of the network's own cost.
MU per transfer a charger may put into a crafting tablet.
Jobs one player's tablet requests may have planned and waiting for a CPU at once; asking again for the same item replaces its job, and requests beyond this are refused.
Whether the online members of a requester's team also get the toast when a crafting job the requester started finishes or stops. The requester always gets it (unless they turned the toasts off).
Show a toast when a crafting job you started finishes, stops or is cancelled by someone else. Off hides them; the terminal's jobs tab still shows its badge.
maxtech_storage.configuration.devices.di: MU each dimension bridge takes from its network every tick while it is active.

MU every operation that crosses a dimension through a dimension bridge costs the network on top of its usual cost: each wireless insert or extract, uplink store, belt refill, mail stack and request board delivery.
maxtech_storage.configuration.devices.ne: Chunks the network anchors of one team keep loaded together: their networks' controllers, drives, energy cells and anchors and the cables between them. 0 turns anchors off.
maxtech_storage.configuration.display.ma: Most display panels along each side of one wall screen; larger groups split into several.
maxtech_storage.configuration.display.up: Fewest ticks between two value updates a display screen sends to the players who see it. Updates go only to players within view distance and only when the value changed.
maxtech_storage.configuration.energy.cel: MU a tier-1 energy storage block holds for its network.
MU one transfer into or out of a tier-1 energy storage block may move, from neighbours and from its network's surplus. The network itself drains it without a limit.
MU a tier-2 energy storage block holds for its network.
MU one transfer into or out of a tier-2 energy storage block may move, from neighbours and from its network's surplus. The network itself drains it without a limit.
MU a tier-3 energy storage block holds for its network.
MU one transfer into or out of a tier-3 energy storage block may move, from neighbours and from its network's surplus. The network itself drains it without a limit.
maxtech_storage.configuration.history.ma: Most values recorded on one network at a time: each history chart display and each recorded pinned value is one. A series keeps 480 numbers (3.75 KiB in memory and in the save); recorders past the limit record nothing and say so.
maxtech_storage.configuration.history.mi: Fewest ticks between two samples of a recorded value (history chart displays, pinned values). A chart set to a shorter interval records at this one. Each sample is one read on the network's scheduler; nothing runs between samples.
maxtech_storage.configuration.history.pi: Ticks between two samples of a Logic Controller's recorded pinned values; 1200 (a minute) keeps four hours in full and 24 hours in six-minute steps. Never below minIntervalTicks.
Most pinned values one Logic Controller records for the sparklines in its rule detail, in rule order; they count against maxSeriesPerNetwork. 0 records none.
mB each of an interface's three fluid stock tanks holds; a fluid stock slot keeps at most this much filled.
maxtech_storage.configuration.ioPort.ope: Operations an IO port makes per tick while it unloads or loads a cell, before speed cards; each moves one batch (network.batch) of one kind.
maxtech_storage.configuration.ioPort.spe: What each speed card in an IO port multiplies its operations per tick by.
maxtech_storage.configuration.loadSheddi: Below this, devices of power priority 2 (high) pause; 0 never.
Below this, devices of power priority 4 (low) pause.
Below this, devices of power priority 3 (normal) pause.
Below this, devices of power priority 5 (optional) pause.
Paused devices resume once the MU is this many percent above their threshold, so they do not flicker on and off around it.

Load shedding: when a network's stored MU falls below a threshold, in percent of its capacity, its devices of that power priority and every less important one pause until the MU is back at the threshold plus resumeMargin. Essential devices (priority 1) never pause; 0 turns a threshold off. Networks with a creative energy source never shed.
maxtech_storage.configuration.logic.cros: Extra action points a rule pays for each action on another network, on top of the action's own: finding the network by name, its access answer and the devices' access checks there.
Extra checks a rule pays for each read of another network (a label like intake@North Base), on top of the read's own cost: finding the network by name and its access answer.
maxtech_storage.configuration.logic.disp: Fewest ticks between two texts a Logic Controller writes to one display, so a value that changes every tick cannot flood players with updates. A text written sooner waits and shows when the time is up.
maxtech_storage.configuration.logic.forE: Most items one run of a rule goes through over all its "For each" nodes. Each item costs the checks of the nodes it runs; a run stops here, or earlier when the team's checks run out, and its why line says so.
maxtech_storage.configuration.logic.hist: Change history entries kept per rule: who saved, reverted, switched or added it, when, and what changed. Older entries are dropped; saved with the controller. 0 keeps no history.
maxtech_storage.configuration.logic.maxG: Graphs one Logic Controller holds and runs. Graphs past the limit are kept but do not run.
maxtech_storage.configuration.logic.maxI: Longest graph text (mtlogic1:...) a player may import into a Logic Controller, in characters. A 64-node graph is about 2,000 characters; longer texts are refused before they are read.
maxtech_storage.configuration.logic.maxN: Most nodes one graph of a Logic Controller may hold. A larger graph is kept but paused with an error until it is made smaller.
maxtech_storage.configuration.logic.maxP: Node values one rule may pin in the node editor; pinned values show in the rule's detail on the controller screen while it is open. 0 turns pinning off.
maxtech_storage.configuration.logic.maxR: How deep graphs may run each other ("Run another rule") in one chain: a graph run by a graph that was itself run counts two, and so on. Circles are refused before they run.
maxtech_storage.configuration.logic.maxV: Shared variables one Logic Controller holds for its graphs. A graph setting a new one past the limit is refused (the why line says so); existing ones still change.
maxtech_storage.configuration.logic.play: Ticks between two looks for players near a device, for graphs with a "Player nearby" node. No event says a player moved, so a controller looks on this timer while such a graph runs, and not at all otherwise.
Largest radius in blocks a "Player nearby" node looks around; a larger setting is cut to this.
maxtech_storage.configuration.logic.remo: MU a logic remote holds. It charges in any FE charger; one that cannot pay an operation shows only its last known notices.
MU a logic remote spends each time it pauses or resumes a rule. Reading notices and rules is free while the remote holds at least this much.
MU per transfer a charger may put into a logic remote.
Show a new notice of a network as a toast while a logic remote bound to it is in your inventory and in range. Off keeps the remote quiet; its screen still lists the notices.
maxtech_storage.configuration.logic.team: Action points per second the logic of one team may use, apart from its checks: each action a rule sends costs about 1 point per microsecond it takes the server (a switch 2, a move of items 12, so 600 allow 50 moves a second). A rule that can act waits for the next second when they are used up.
Checks per second the logic of one team may use: the nodes rules evaluate and sensor reads. Work over the budget waits for the next second; player work is never held back.
maxtech_storage.configuration.logic.toas: Show the toasts logic graphs send to your team. Off hides them for you only; the notices still reach the network's log and chat.
maxtech_storage.configuration.machines.e: MU each Storage machine's buffer holds, the fuel generator's included.

showcase.maxtech_storage.bridges.name: AE2 and RS bridges
showcase.maxtech_storage.bridges.summary: A Storage network with a bridge to a powered AE2 grid (west) and one to a Refined Storage network (east), each stocked with items of its own, so each side lists the other's items. A mod that is not loaded gets a sign naming its dev-run flag (-PwithAe2=true, -PwithRs=true).
showcase.maxtech_storage.cables.name: Cables
showcase.maxtech_storage.cables.summary: Every cable look in tiers 1 to 4, a red cable and a cable under a stone brick facade.
showcase.maxtech_storage.channels.name: Channels, hubs
showcase.maxtech_storage.channels.summar: A tier-1 cable (8 channels) with ten terminals on it, so the two placed last are offline and name the full cable; hubs of tiers 3, 2 and 1 (64, 32 and 16 channels) nested on one branch, each with three terminals; a second controller in the same network on standby; and at the back a network without a controller, which holds 8 channels in all.
showcase.maxtech_storage.core.name: Core network
showcase.maxtech_storage.core.summary: A controller of two blocks with upgrade cards, a security module on the cable, a tier-1 energy cell, two drives (item cells of four tiers, a fluid cell), terminal, pattern terminal, network chest and a storage chest.
showcase.maxtech_storage.crafting.name: Autocrafting
showcase.maxtech_storage.crafting.summar: CPU clusters of tiers 1 to 3, a pattern provider on a furnace (raw iron to ingot) and one on a crafting assembler (planks to sticks), a stock keeper keeping 32 sticks and an export port with a crafting card that smelts iron ingots into its chest.
showcase.maxtech_storage.energy.name: Energy
showcase.maxtech_storage.energy.summary: A network run on MU from a fuel generator alone, no creative source: the generator uses no channel (nor do the cells) and fills the controller's buffer first, then energy cells of tiers 1 to 3 take what is left. A terminal and a drive on the cable, and a chest with a signal probe and a network analyzer for the readouts. Another mod's FE block next to a cell would feed the network at Lib's FE rate.
showcase.maxtech_storage.logic.name: Logic
showcase.maxtech_storage.logic.summary: Logic Controller with eight ready graphs: one per action, one on a sensor crossing and one with a counter and latch. Labelled ports, drive and condition switches in logic mode, a sensor block on a chest, a sensor part on a lever and a display wall showing logic notices. The lever on the controller turns the intake port on and sets the drive's priority, the button on the outbox port moves 16 cobblestone out, three flips of the lever above the cable light the latch lamp, and sticks are crafted whenever fewer than 16 are stored.
showcase.maxtech_storage.machines.name: Machines
showcase.maxtech_storage.machines.summar: Fuel generator with coal feeding a lithograph, fabricator and assembler, each with a full buffer and inputs for one recipe.
showcase.maxtech_storage.ports.name: Ports, devices
showcase.maxtech_storage.ports.summary: Block port and port part importing from chests, interface stocking cobblestone, item P2P pair fed by a hopper, condition switch on a lamp, display wall graphing cobblestone, placer, breaker and collector on the cable.
showcase.maxtech_storage.priority.name: Priority
showcase.maxtech_storage.priority.summar: An import port fed by a hopper and a chest, a drive at priority 2147483647, a bulk drive at 0 and a drive at -100: new items go to the highest priority with room, and a kind already stored goes where it is first.
showcase.maxtech_storage.subnet.name: Subnet, antennas
showcase.maxtech_storage.subnet.summary: Subnet controller in merged mode with its own drive and terminal, a paired antenna pair with a terminal on the far end, and a bound, charged wireless terminal in the chest.
showcase.maxtech_storage.tools.name: Tools
showcase.maxtech_storage.tools.summary: Chests with every Storage tool (bound and charged where that matters), bulk drive and void items; a bulk drive on the network.
toast.maxtech_storage.crafting.provider_: Crafting held up: a provider is locked
tooltip.maxtech_storage.blueprint.empty: Use on a device to copy its settings
tooltip.maxtech_storage.blueprint.use: Use on the same kind to paste, sneak-use to paste along a row; sneak-use in the air to clear
tooltip.maxtech_storage.bulk_drive.capac: Up to %s items of one kind
tooltip.maxtech_storage.bulk_drive.help: Sneak-use with an empty hand to take a stack
tooltip.maxtech_storage.cable_layer: Use on two blocks to lay storage cable between them, taken from the bound network. Sneak-use on a controller to bind, on a storage cable to pick its kind and colour; sneak-use in the air drops the start. Charge in any FE charger.

tooltip.maxtech_storage.efficiency_modul: Lithograph, fabricator, assembler: runs cost less MU
tooltip.maxtech_storage.network_analyzer: Hold to read the storage block you look at; use on a block for the full report and its route, sneak-use for the network around you. Use in the air with a processor or storage cell in the other hand to analyse it for research points.
tooltip.maxtech_storage.network_goggles: Wear to see the storage network you look at: zone, channel use and route in the action bar, and the network around you through walls. Charge in any FE charger.
tooltip.maxtech_storage.p2p.linker_empty: Sneak-use on a link to make it an input
tooltip.maxtech_storage.pattern.unreadab: Unusable: names an unknown entry (mod missing)
tooltip.maxtech_storage.precision_module: Lithograph: more dies from each printed wafer
tooltip.maxtech_storage.puzzle_cartridge: Use it to solve a research puzzle. Solving it uses the cartridge up and gives your team part of a skip token's points
Blank: using it picks a puzzle
tooltip.maxtech_storage.quarantine_tag: Use on a storage network you own (or as an operator) to freeze it: nothing moves, nothing is lost. Use again to lift it.
tooltip.maxtech_storage.research_notes: Read to give your team research points.
tooltip.maxtech_storage.research_scanner: Use on any block: the first scan of each block type gives your team research points.
Use on a ghost to build it from the network of a carried wireless terminal
Use on two corners to copy the devices between them
Use on a block to place a ghost; sneak-use in the air to turn it, sneak-use on a ghost to remove it, sneak-use elsewhere to copy anew
tooltip.maxtech_storage.signal_probe: Use on a storage cable or device to bind it, then use in the air to graph how many of its channels are in use
tooltip.maxtech_storage.speed_module: Lithograph, fabricator, assembler: faster runs for more MU
tooltip.maxtech_storage.storage_block.ho: Items and fluids; keeps them when broken
tooltip.maxtech_storage.storage_block.in: Inactive: its cell is in use elsewhere or unreadable
tooltip.maxtech_storage.storage_manual: Cables, drives, cells, terminals and research
tooltip.maxtech_storage.trace_pen: Sneak-use on a storage cable or device to mark the start, then use on another block of the same network to trace the route between them. Sneak-use in the air to drop the start.
tooltip.maxtech_storage.usage_report_boo: Use for a report on your team's storage networks in this dimension, or on a network block for that network: devices, limits, bytes and who placed what.
tooltip.maxtech_storage.view_filter.blan: Blank: use it in hand to set it up
tooltip.maxtech_storage.void_module: Lithograph, fabricator, assembler: several runs at once for more MU; fits beside another module
tooltip.maxtech_storage.wireless.bound: Bound to the controller at %s %s %s in %s
tooltip.maxtech_storage.wrench: Sneak-use: pick up a device with its contents and settings, or take a part off a cable
tooltip.maxtech_storage.zone_painter: Use on a storage cable to paint it as a zone border, again to clear it: a painted cable always starts a zone of its own. Use in the air to see the painted borders near you.
